problems.title: The Jacobi bound needs fixed position-specific randomness
problems.source_location: Section 3, PDF p.4; cited Song et al. Proposition 1
claim: The paragraph writes sampled parallel updates and an at-most-\(N\) iteration bound without specifying coupling between iterations.
analysis: At \(N=1\), a uniform binary token with fresh independent draws has path \(0\to1\to0\) with probability \(1/4\), changing beyond one update. Path \(0\to0\to1\) also has probability \(1/4\), so a coincidental equality is not an absorbing fixed point. In contrast, draw one \(U_1\) once and use the same inverse-CDF map each time: the first update settles the token. In general, fixed \(U_i\) and causal maps \(G_i(x_{<i},U_i)\) settle the first \(j\) positions after \(j\) updates by induction; after \(N\) updates the vector equals the sequential ancestral sample and remains fixed.
result: The unconditional fresh-sampling interpretation is false, but the notation does not establish that the authors implement it. The separate speculative acceptance/progress rule and model quality are not refuted.
repair: Specify reuse of the same random variate for each global token position, or a deterministic map/tie rule. An initially fixed seed that advances on every update is insufficient; an additional equality-check evaluation may be needed unless the known iteration bound is used directly.
